title: The light above (7.10)
hookLine: he enters within and sees a light above his mind
tomorrow: if everything God made is good, where does the rot come from?

cards: When a boss says a decision is above your pay grade, nobody looks at the ceiling. Above can mean something besides higher up. Augustine needs that other meaning.
Once God isn't a body up in the sky, where does he look? Inside. The books, he says, warned him to return to himself, so he went into his own depths, with God as his guide.
And there, above his own mind, he saw a light. Then comes an odd line: it wasn't above him the way oil floats above water. So what kind of above is it?

teach.b: First, the way in. Not the stars this time. His own mind, with the eye of his soul, as he puts it.
Second, what the light was not.
Not the ordinary light anyone can see. Not a bigger, brighter version of it, filling everything. Other, he says, far other.
Third, the puzzle solved. It wasn't above his mind the way oil sits on water, or the sky stretches over the earth.

It was above him because it made him, and he was below it because he was made by it. Above means maker, not altitude. A little like an author and a story: the author isn't on a higher shelf, but the story comes from her.
Fourth, a name. He says he heard, as if from far off, the name God gives Moses at the burning bush, in the Douay-Rheims: "I AM WHO AM."
He heard it the way the heart hears, and he could sooner doubt he was alive than doubt that truth is. And he says he trembled, with love and with awe.
Here's one to tell a friend tonight: Augustine's Latin for what he saw is lucem incommutabilem, the light that doesn't change. Notice the order. Within first: he had to come home to himself.
Then above: the light was not himself.

how: Catholic spiritual writers describe prayer as recollection, gathering oneself inward, and then turning toward God; Augustine's ascent in book seven is one of the texts they draw on.

o: a bright light in the sky over the city
the calm of a mind emptied of all thought
a light above the mind, because it made him

games.q: within, then above — tap the pairs.
p: the name he heard from afar

s: Augustine found the light by looking up at the night sky
he went inward first, into his own depths, and saw it above his mind.
the light was above his mind the way oil floats on water
he says no: it was above because it made him.
Augustine says he trembled with love and with awe
and he could sooner doubt he was alive than doubt that truth is.

games.q: a friend says meditation is just about finding your true self, full stop. by Confessions 7.10, what's Augustine's next step?
o: a light above the self, which made it.
nothing more: the self is the light.
back outside, to look at the stars.
games.why: Augustine goes within, then above. The light he finds is not himself; it's above him because it made him.

practice: Sit tall and let your eyes rest on your hands in your lap: notice your breath, your body, the thoughts passing through.
Then, slowly, lift your gaze to the highest point in the room, not to find God up there, but as your body's way of saying above. If you pray, you can rest in the name he heard: I AM WHO AM.

wordCard.voice: The light above. What Augustine saw within: not over his mind like oil on water, but above it as its maker.

orig.note: Latin: the unchangeable light, Augustine's words for what he saw above his mind in Confessions 7.10.

carryVoice: Within, then above: going inward is the road, not the end of it. See you tomorrow.
